summary: Today's strongest theme is distrust of vendor-controlled settings: AI chat training toggles flipping back on, Windows 11 setup forcing accounts, and car head units that ignore the user. Self-hosted web archiving and YouTube-without-the-algorithm on TV also came up repeatedly. Reddit, X and Bluesky were blocked today, so every source below is from Hacker News.

ideas.title: AI Opt-Out Watchdog
ideas.oneLiner: An extension that checks your ChatGPT, Gemini and other AI data-sharing toggles every day and alerts you the moment one flips back to 'train on my chats'.
ideas.problem: A team found 'Improve the model for everyone' had been silently re-enabled in Codex after they had all turned it off. Another user says Mistral reset every staff slider to 'on' during a policy change. On Gemini, commenters say there is no real opt-out other than losing chat history, so people discover settings too late.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers, freelancers and small teams who paste client code or private documents into AI tools and have to prove to clients or employers that sharing is off.
ideas.monetization: Free for 2 providers; ₹199–399/month (or $4–5) for unlimited accounts, change alerts by email/Telegram, and a team dashboard with an exportable audit log.
mvp: Detect and read the data-controls page state for ChatGPT and Gemini while the user is logged in (read-only, nothing leaves the browser)
Daily background check with a desktop notification if training or human review is switched on
One-click link to the exact settings page for each provider
Local change log with timestamps for audit purposes
Add Claude, Mistral and Codex settings pages after the first release

competitors.name: Provider settings pages (ChatGPT Data Controls, Gemini Keep Activity)
competitors.gap: They only show state when you open them manually, and users report the state changing without notice.

competitors.name: General privacy dashboards / manual checklists
competitors.gap: No tool I found monitors AI-training toggles across several vendors and alerts on change; this is checked by hand.

None of us knowingly opted back in.

ideas.title: Archive-It-Yourself Clipper
ideas.oneLiner: A local-first app plus browser extension that saves full copies of pages you care about from your own logged-in browser and keeps them searchable, with no ArchiveBox server to maintain.
ideas.problem: A thread on backing up websites drew 600+ points. People who run ArchiveBox say queues fill with failed scans and maintenance gets annoying, and server-side capture fails on sites behind Cloudflare. They stitch together Linkding, SingleFile and other tools by hand, and several people have built their own small tools to fill the gap.
ideas.targetUsers: Researchers, writers, developers and heavy bookmarkers who have seen link rot eat their saved links and don't want to run a home server.
ideas.monetization: Free local app; $4/month or $39/year for encrypted sync to the user's own S3/Drive bucket, full-text search across devices and scheduled re-checks for dead links. One-time $29 licence as an alternative.
mvp: One-click capture in the browser using the user's own session (works for paywalled and Cloudflare-protected pages)
Single-file HTML plus screenshot stored in a plain folder
Full-text search and tags
Dead-link checker that tells you which saved bookmarks are now 404
Optional sync to the user's own cloud storage

competitors.name: ArchiveBox
competitors.gap: Commenters report failed-scan queues, upkeep burden, and trouble capturing sites that block server-side crawlers.

competitors.name: SingleFile
competitors.gap: Great capture, but no library, search or sync of its own; people pair it with Linkding or Karakeep.

competitors.name: Linkding / Karakeep / Linkwarden
competitors.gap: Need a self-hosted server; users describe gluing several pieces together.

ideas.title: Subs-Only YouTube for TV
ideas.oneLiner: A tvOS and Android TV app that shows only your subscriptions, newest first, with duration filters and no recommendations.
ideas.problem: People say YouTube's recommendations are poor but hard to turn off, and that limiting the app to subscriptions is 'annoyingly difficult'. Many watch on an Apple TV, where the community-made alternatives are web-only, so they have nowhere to go. Others ask for sort-by-recency and duration filters.
ideas.targetUsers: Paying YouTube users who watch mostly on a living-room TV and want a calm, subscriptions-only feed.
ideas.monetization: One-time $9.99 or $2/month; free tier limited to 20 channels. No ads, no tracking.
mvp: Import channels from a pasted list or a Google Takeout subscriptions file
Chronological feed with duration and 'watched' filters
Remote-friendly TV UI with large thumbnails
Resume position and a simple watch-later queue
Phone companion for adding channels

competitors.name: SmartTube / Grayjay
competitors.gap: A commenter uses Grayjay with the home page disabled, but it is mainly Android and desktop; Apple TV users in the thread have no equivalent.

competitors.name: YouTube app (Subscriptions tab)
competitors.gap: Recommendations dominate the home screen and commenters say limiting it to subscriptions is awkward.

ideas.title: Clean Windows 11 Setup Kit
ideas.oneLiner: A guided installer builder that makes Windows 11 media with a local account, no bundled extras and a classic-style shell, and keeps working when Microsoft changes the tricks.
ideas.problem: Commenters on a Windows 11 thread say they won't use it while an online account is required, and others want a classic NT4/2000-style interface badly enough to say they would pay. Users who do reinstall piece together command-prompt tricks or unofficial guides to avoid the extras.
ideas.targetUsers: Gamers with a Windows box, small-office admins and people refurbishing PCs for family who want a plain, predictable Windows.
ideas.monetization: Free basic builder; $19 one-time Pro with presets for multiple PCs, unattended answer files and a classic-shell option.
mvp: Pick the official ISO and write a USB drive
Answer-file generator: local account, privacy defaults, region and username preset
Optional removal list for bundled apps with a preview
Check-after-update tool that tells you if a Windows update re-enabled anything
Saved profiles for repeat installs

competitors.name: Rufus
competitors.gap: Offers account and requirement bypass options, but search results note it does more than needed and its methods depend on Microsoft not closing loopholes.

competitors.name: NTLite
competitors.gap: Powerful but paid and aimed at experts; forum threads show local-account support needs manual settings per release.

competitors.name: massgrave.dev guides
competitors.gap: A commenter found it helpful for getting LTSC, but it is guides rather than a one-click builder.

ideas.title: Car Autoplay Blocker
ideas.oneLiner: An Android app that stops your phone's music or podcast from auto-resuming when it connects to a car's Bluetooth or USB, and handles the car's forced Play commands.
ideas.problem: Several drivers say their car head unit sends a Play command every time the phone connects, or restarts audio the moment they pause on the phone. Fixing the car's software is not possible for most owners.
ideas.targetUsers: Android drivers with older or mid-range cars whose head units can't be configured.
ideas.monetization: Free with one profile; ₹99 or $1.99 one-time for per-car profiles and rules like 'allow only after I press play'.
mvp: Detect connection to a chosen car (Bluetooth device or USB)
Pause and ignore Play commands for the first N seconds after connecting
Per-car profile with an 'ignore external play' switch
Quick toggle tile in the notification shade
Optional hold timer after the user pauses manually

competitors.name: Bluetooth auto-play apps and Tasker
competitors.gap: Existing automation tools are mostly built to start music on connect, not block it, and need manual rule building (I did not verify specific listings).

ideas.title: One-Tap Usual Order
ideas.oneLiner: A chat or widget that re-places your regular food order at your usual time, so you skip the delivery-app browsing and upsells.
ideas.problem: In a thread about AI agents and DoorDash, commenters say they order the same thing every time and would happily delegate it, and one calls delivery apps 'dark-pattern-filled' with constant upsells. Skeptics point out that the labelled data in the apps is poor.
ideas.targetUsers: Office workers and families who repeat the same lunch or grocery order weekly.
ideas.monetization: Free for 1 saved order; ₹149/month for several saved orders, schedule prompts and price alerts. Depends on deep-link or partner access, which is the main risk.
mvp: Save a 'usual' order from a restaurant's link or a past order screenshot
Lunchtime notification: 'Order the usual?' with one tap to open the prefilled cart
Order history and typical-spend view
Skip-week and swap-item options

competitors.name: Delivery apps' own Reorder features
competitors.gap: Users in the thread still complain about the interfaces, upsells and ads they must get through.

competitors.name: Voice assistants (Alexa reorder)
competitors.gap: Commenters say they mainly use it for paper towels and toilet paper, not hot food.
